blocks.text: HANGS Construction Services LLC. Invented procedures for a software demonstration.

Each payroll register is booked from Brookline's journal: field crews to 1400 Construction in Progress, job 27-05, cost code 01-100, and office and site management to 6000 Salaries & Wages, at total cost. The funding debit on the bank statement must equal the register's total cost, and 2130, 2140, 2145 and 2190 must clear to zero once the funding is booked.

When an employee leaves, the payroll lead end-dates the employee in Brookline before the next payroll is processed. Final pay covers work through the last day worked. Any pay after that date is an overpayment and is recovered.

Hourly employees are paid 1.5 times their straight-time rate for hours over 40 in a workweek, as the union wage and fringe schedule requires. An underpayment is corrected on the next payroll and accrued at month-end.

Brookline withholds and deposits federal income tax, social security and Medicare, employee and employer shares, on the semiweekly schedule, and holds the Washington premiums for the quarterly return. The tax liability report must equal the registers to the cent.
PAY-5 Union Dues, Benefits and Garnishments

Union dues and the employer's fringe contributions are remitted to the trust each month; 401(k) deferrals within three business days of each pay date. Each garnishment is remitted to the agency within seven business days after the pay date, as the order requires. Amounts withheld and not remitted are a liability until they are paid.

The Controller reviews this reconciliation and every proposed entry. Entries are posted only after that review, by the person who posts journal entries, and payroll corrections are made in Brookline by the payroll lead.

passages.q: Must HANGS Construction Services file Form 940 for 2026?
passages.a: You're subject to FUTA tax in 2026 on the wages you pay employees who aren't farmworkers or household workers if: you paid wages of $1,500 or more in any calendar quarter in 2025 or 2026, or you had one or more employees for at least some part of a day in any 20 or more different weeks in 2025 or 20 or more different weeks in 2026.

passages.q: What are the 2026 FUTA rate, wage base and credit?
passages.a: For 2026, the FUTA tax rate is 6.0%. The tax applies to the first $7,000 you pay to each employee as wages during the year. ... The credit may be as much as 5.4% of FUTA taxable wages. If you're entitled to the maximum 5.4% credit, the FUTA tax rate after credit is 0.6%.

passages.q: Do employees' 401(k) deferrals come off FUTA wages?
passages.a: Elective employee contributions and deferrals to a plan containing a qualified cash or deferred compensation arrangement (401(k)). Generally exempt, but see section 402(g) for limitation. Taxable. Taxable.

passages.q: When is the Q3 2026 Form 941 due?
passages.a: Your Form 941 is due by the last day of the month that follows the end of the quarter. ... 3. July, August, September September 30 October 31 ... If you made timely deposits in full payment of your taxes for the quarter, you may file by the 10th day of the 2nd month that follows the end of the quarter. ... If any due date for filing falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday, you may file your return on the next business day.

passages.q: Which employees are counted on line 1, and what goes on lines 2 and 3?
passages.a: Enter the number of employees on your payroll for the pay period including March 12, June 12, September 12, or December 12, for the quarter indicated at the top of Form 941. ... Enter amounts on line 2 that would also be included in box 1 of your employees’ Forms W-2. ... Enter the federal income tax you withheld (or were required to withhold) from your employees on this quarter’s wages, tips, taxable fringe benefits, and supplemental unemployment compensation benefits.

passages.q: Which wages go on line 5a, and where does Social Security stop for each employee?
passages.a: The social security tax rate is 6.2% each for the employee and employer. The social security wage base limit is $184,500. ... For 2026, the rate of social security tax on taxable wages is 6.2% (0.062) each for the employer and employee. Stop paying social security tax on and entering an employee’s wages on line 5a when the employee’s taxable wages and tips reach $184,500 for the year. ... line 5a (column 1) x 0.124 line 5a (column 2)

sources.title: General Instructions for Forms W-2 and W-3 (2026)

passages.q: When are the 2026 Forms W-2 and W-3 due, and must they be e-filed?
passages.a: The due date for filing 2026 Forms W-2 ... and W-3 ... with the SSA is February 1, 2027, whether you file using paper forms or electronically. ... Generally, you must furnish Copies B, C, and 2 of Form W-2 to your employees by February 1, 2027. ... You must e-file Forms W-2 ... if you are required to file at least 10 information returns.

passages.q: What goes in box 1, and are the 401(k) deferrals and Washington Paid Leave premiums in it?
passages.a: Box 1-Wages, tips, other compensation. Show the total taxable wages, tips, and other compensation that you paid to your employee during the year. However, do not include elective deferrals (such as employee contributions to a section 401(k) or 403(b) plan) ... You must include the employee contribution and the employer voluntary payment as wages on the Form W-2.

passages.q: What are the 2026 Social Security limits for boxes 3 and 4, and what goes in boxes 5 and 6?
passages.a: The total of boxes 3 and 7 cannot exceed $184,500 (2026 maximum social security wage base). ... For 2026, the amount should not exceed $11,439 ... there is no wage base limit for Medicare tax ... an employer is required to withhold a 0.9% Additional Medicare Tax on any Federal Insurance Contributions Act (FICA) wages ... in excess of $200,000 in a calendar year.

checks.detail: The October 10 register cost $96,412.18; Brookline debited $96,412.18 that day, the statement's "ACH debit BROOKLINE PAYROLL SERVICES", and GL 1010 shows the same. The October 24 register cost $97,055.64; Brookline debited $97,055.64 that day, the statement's "ACH debit BROOKLINE PAYROLL SERVICES", and GL 1010 shows the same. Register less bank: $0.00.

checks.title: Tie the payroll taxes to the tax liability report and the deposits
checks.detail: Every employee's social security and Medicare recompute at 6.2% and 1.45%. For October 10, federal taxes of $21,639.62 were deposited October 15, before the October 16 due date, and $1,049.29 of Washington premiums is held for the quarterly return. For October 24, federal taxes of $21,783.80 were deposited October 29, before the October 30 due date, and $1,056.43 of Washington premiums is held for the quarterly return. The tax liability report agrees with the registers to the cent (PAY-4).

checks.title: Tie dues, fringe, 401(k), medical and garnishments to the remittances
checks.detail: Union dues recompute at 2.25% of each member's gross and fringe at $2.30 an hour worked, as the wage schedule requires. For both pay dates, dues and fringe, 401(k) and medical premiums agree with Brookline's remittance report and with what was funded. The garnishments do not all reach the agency.

checks.title: Trace the October 24 garnishment to the agency
checks.detail: $312.50 withheld from E-115 on October 24 under order WA-DEMO-000417 was never sent to the State Support Registry. The order requires $312.50 each pay period, remitted within 7 business days. The October 24 register withheld it, Brookline's funding took it from the bank, and GL 2145 was cleared as if it had been paid. Brookline's remittance report says otherwise: "Not remitted: payee remittance ID missing in Brookline". The October 10 payment went out on time. This one was due November 3 and is past due. AJ-01 puts the obligation back in 2145 Garnishments Payable and the money Brookline holds in 1280. Have Brookline add the remittance ID and pay it today, and keep the proof of payment with the order.

checks.title: Test every overtime line against 1.5 times the straight-time rate
checks.detail: E-108 worked 6 overtime hours paid at $38.50; the schedule requires $57.75. The union schedule pays 1.5 times the straight-time rate over 40 hours a week. E-108 is a carpenter at $38.50, so overtime is $57.75 an hour; the October 24 register paid $38.50. 6 hours short by $19.25 is $115.50 owed to the employee, plus $8.83 of employer social security and Medicare. Of 14 overtime lines in October, this is the only one paid at the wrong rate. AJ-03 accrues the cost to job 27-05; pay it on the November 7 payroll and fix the overtime rate on this employee's record in Brookline.
checks.source: 02 HR/Union Wage and Fringe Schedule - June 1, 2026.pdf

checks.title: Test every employee paid against the roster and the separation notices
checks.detail: E-124 left on October 9 but was paid 80 hours, $2,250.00 gross, on October 24. The separation notice gives October 9 as the last day worked, with final pay on the October 10 payroll, and HR shows the employee as terminated. Brookline still shows the employee as active, so the salary ran again for October 10 to October 23, 2026, a period that starts after the last day. Net pay of $1,784.97 was deposited. The cost to HANGS is $2,597.13: $2,250.00 of wages, $172.13 of employer social security and Medicare and $175.00 of benefits. AJ-02 moves it from 6000 Salaries & Wages to 1260 Payroll Overpayment Receivable. Recover the net pay from the former employee, have Brookline process a wage correction so the taxes come back on the fourth-quarter return, and end-date the employee. The close's RJ-05 accrual was computed from this register and carries $1,298.57 of this person's cost (5 of 10 workdays); reduce it by that amount.

checks.title: Add up the open items
checks.detail: October payroll of $193,467.82 ties to the ledger and the bank, taxes and withholdings tie out, and 3 exceptions need a person: garnishment not remitted, terminated employee still paid, overtime paid at straight time. 3 entries proposed for $3,033.96. Nothing was posted.
